findingDetails.title: Visual-review intent does not load the accessibility reference it cites
findingDetails.claim: WEB_VISUAL_HIERARCHY loads three files but its review pass cites web-accessibility-patterns.md for seven checks, and the router rule says a row loads what it resolves and nothing more.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether another intent loads the file in the same bundle; WEB_A11Y does, but WEB_VISUAL_HIERARCHY does not, and the review pass is the only section that cites those anchors.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The A-anchors may be optional follow-on reads; the pass does not label them optional, and the router's load rule forbids loading outside the row.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the pass is amended to mark the A-anchors as follow-on reads outside the intent.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The three-file map is the only stage-two row for this intent; seven A-anchor links in the review pass point at a file not in it.

findingDetails.title: Hub canary never exercises the new visual vocabulary
findingDetails.claim: The sk-code canary has nine cases and no prompt containing a code-frontend-visual keyword, so the regression harness cannot catch the visual-review route failure or a future tie-break change.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked the surface-hint unit test, which covers the pre-existing css-cascade-layers family and the near-miss exclusions; it does not cover the new visual phrases.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The playbook scenario covers one new intent; it is a packet-level replay, not the hub route gold the canary protects.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: None at P2; it becomes P1 when combined with an active routing failure that the canary should have caught.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Parsed all nine canary cases; none of their prompts contains a code-frontend-visual keyword.
